ask: Announce our new Lisbon office on LinkedIn, X and Threads. Same news, but write it right for each one.

steps.why: Limits once for the networks named: X 280, Threads 500, LinkedIn 3,000. Each version is counted against its own network.
The three account ids. Any account marked for reconnecting is named before writing for it.

arguments.content: We've opened an office in Lisbon. Eight of us start there in January, and we're hiring two more.

linkedin.text:
We've opened our second office, in Lisbon.

Eight of us start there in January. Why Lisbon: half our customers are within three hours of it, and the people we want to hire already live there.

We're hiring two engineers. Ask me anything about the team.

x.text: New office: Lisbon. Eight of us start in January, and we're hiring two engineers.

threads.text: We picked Lisbon for our second office. Eight of us move in January. Anyone here worked from there? Tips welcome.

steps.why: Same media, same time, one part each: one post, a fresh text per network in platform_specific, written separately with different first lines. content stays as the fallback. The Threads topic goes in the same call; through platform_specific it needs no use_topic_tag. Saved as a draft: no time, no action.
Read back: metadata.platformSpecific holds each network's text and the topic as Bolta stored them.

say: Saved to Acme as one draft for 3 networks. 1. LinkedIn: (full text) 2. X: (full text) 3. Threads: (full text), topic Startups. Nothing goes out yet. One yes covers all three. Schedule it?
